issues.subject: The first dark miles
issues.text:
Long Run Sunday · {date}

The first dark miles

The clocks go back on Sunday 25 October. We'll have a brighter start and lose the light earlier in the afternoon. Time to dig out the light you put away in April.

Marshes loop, 25 October
Start at the Lea Bridge Road crossing and use the broad path down the east side of the football pitches. Our autumn loop is 12.4 km from the bridge and back. The boardwalk by the filter beds was slick when we went round on Friday. There's a paved bypass marked in the route notes, and the water tap at the pavilion has been turned off for winter.
https://longrunsunday.example/routes/marshes-autumn-loop

Three weeks to the Dock Basin 10K
If you've been doing one speed session a week, Tuesday is a good day for five six-minute stretches at the effort you could keep up for an hour. Jog for two minutes between them. Save the finish-line effort for race day. The last turnaround at Dock Basin is tighter than it looks on the course map, and the organisers have moved it clear of the cobbles.
https://longrunsunday.example/training/three-weeks-to-dock-basin

Field test: Alder Tempo 2
We put 74 km into the Tempo 2 on road and towpath. The shallow tread was fine on wet tarmac, and the outer heel held up better than on the first Tempo. The tongue crept sideways until we used the spare eyelet. The toe box is snug once your feet warm up. If ordering by post, try them indoors in the socks you run in.
https://longrunsunday.example/shoes/alder-tempo-2-wet

See you out there,
Mara Whitcombe, editor

Long Run Sunday · 14 Tern Yard, London E9 5DP

issues.subject: What to run after a half
issues.text:
Long Run Sunday · {date}

What to run after a half

A few of you wrote after the Wandle Half with a faster time than you expected and legs that felt rather worse. Here's what to do with the following Sunday.

Take the short loop
Forty easy minutes is enough for the first weekend back. Start with the person who usually takes the shortest option and go home when they do. Our tester Ben cut through Springfield Park after 5 km and was glad of the hill test: the ups felt fine and the downs still felt like mile twelve. He walked the last slope to the cafe.
https://longrunsunday.example/training/after-the-half

Race notes: Wandle Half
The pack bunched just after the second bridge, where one side of the path was still open to dog walkers. The third water table was moved about 150 metres down the course and was much easier to spot than the first two. There were cups there well after the two-hour pacers came through. Our photos are grouped by crossing if you're looking for yours.
https://longrunsunday.example/races/wandle-half-review

A clip light that stays put
Fieldgate's clip light sat best on the rear strap of a running belt. On the hem of a thin shirt, it bounced and spun towards the body. We got just over five hours on the slow pulse setting after a full charge. The cover over the charging port is small enough that it's worth checking with a fingernail before you go out in rain.
https://longrunsunday.example/kit/fieldgate-clip

See you out there,
Mara Whitcombe, editor

Long Run Sunday · 14 Tern Yard, London E9 5DP

issues.subject: Hills by feel, coffee by the canal
issues.text:
Long Run Sunday · {date}

Hills by feel, coffee by the canal

One of the easier ways to make a Sunday group run miserable is to give everyone the same uphill pace. This week we're working from the length of the slope.

Six climbs at Fairlead Hill
Use the lamppost above the first bend as a marker, or stop when your watch hits forty-five seconds. Space yourselves out on the way down so there's room for walkers and bikes, and let the last runner start first on the next rep. The slope eases near the top. Leave that stretch for the jog home and you'll have something left for the final climb.
https://longrunsunday.example/training/fairlead-six-climbs

North Cut Relay: the handover
The provisional leg times are up with a note about the second exchange. The marshals had to move it beyond the gate after a delivery van parked across the original holding lane. Anyone who timed their own second leg from the gate will find their watch a little short. The volunteer with the yellow clipboard got all four runners from our group across in order.
https://longrunsunday.example/races/north-cut-handover

Trail soles for town miles
We tried the Millbank Track 4 on the towpath out and on the pavement home. It clears soft mud well enough, and the lugs stay quiet on brick. There's a ridge across the arch that became noticeable on the road after about an hour. The shop has a sample pair in each half size through eight and a half if you'd rather try before buying.
https://longrunsunday.example/shoes/light-trail-road-test

See you out there,
Mara Whitcombe, editor

Long Run Sunday · 14 Tern Yard, London E9 5DP

issues.subject: The steady bit in a long run
issues.text:
Long Run Sunday · {date}

The steady bit in a long run

On group runs the middle miles tend to speed up on their own. If you want a steady finish, it helps to decide where it starts while everyone is still talking.

The last twenty minutes
Take an easy route out that lets you turn somewhere obvious. Once you're back on even ground, bring the effort up just far enough that you're talking in shorter sentences. Give it five minutes before you glance at the pace. On our loop the service bridge is a good start marker, and getting back there first gives everyone a chance to settle after the slope.
https://longrunsunday.example/training/steady-finish-twenty

Moor Lane 10: the soft verge
The race photos confirm what it felt like underfoot. The worn strip at the edge of Moor Lane was the driest line on the way out, but it didn't hold up by the time the last wave came back. Several people lost a shoe there. Stay wide at that bend on a training recce, and mind the gap between the stile and the fence.
https://longrunsunday.example/races/moor-lane-ten

The shorts with room for a key
The centre pocket on the Eliot Five fits a door key and folded card without either sitting against a hip bone. A phone stays in, though it pulled the waistband down on one of our testers. The thin lining dried before the outer fabric. If you carry a phone over a long distance, bring it when you try the shorts and jog a few steps.
https://longrunsunday.example/kit/eliot-pocket-shorts

See you out there,
Mara Whitcombe, editor

Long Run Sunday · 14 Tern Yard, London E9 5DP

issues.subject: A first run with the group
issues.text:
Long Run Sunday · {date}

A first run with the group

Our beginners' table gets about the same three questions every week. Here's what the first hour looks like, plus a local race report and a small kit fix.

Where the slower group meets
Look for the two marshals in green at the lower gate by the lock. We start the 5 km jog at 08:15 and wait at each of the two crossings. The route is a figure eight, so the halfway point takes you past the gate again. Anyone who wants to finish there can grab a layer from the bag pile without keeping the group waiting.
https://longrunsunday.example/clubs/first-sunday-at-the-lock

The Bow Cut four-miler
The junior loop started first this year, which left a clear path for both groups by the time the adults came through the lock. The field stretched out naturally on the first ramp, and all but the first few finishers had someone beside them on the home straight. The temporary ramp at the turn was slippery under leaves. It's been taken out since the race.
https://longrunsunday.example/races/bow-cut-four-mile

When a heel keeps slipping
Try the spare pair of eyelets before swapping out a shoe you've already worn. Feed each end through the last hole on its own side to make a loop, cross through the loops, and pull down towards the toes. A little tension does it. If you have to crank the laces to keep the heel in place, the shoe is probably too roomy at the back.
https://longrunsunday.example/kit/laces-and-slipping-heels

See you out there,
Mara Whitcombe, editor

Long Run Sunday · 14 Tern Yard, London E9 5DP

issues.subject: Carry water for the route you take
issues.text:
Long Run Sunday · {date}

Carry water for the route you take

Two people came to the pavilion on Sunday expecting to refill and found a padlock. We checked the other taps along the canal and updated the route sheet.

Refill points between the locks
The bottle filler on the outside wall of the rowing club is reachable from the path. There's another beside the shelter at the rec, about four minutes off the direct route via the gate on Mildmay Lane. The little tap marked on the old map by the boat shed has gone. We timed the rec detour from both sides and added the shorter approach to the sheet.
https://longrunsunday.example/routes/lock-to-lock-water

Fuel before the footbridge
It's easy to keep a snack in your pocket until you need it and then discover you don't feel much like chewing. On a run over ninety minutes, try opening it well before the climb or awkward crossing. For the canal loop we use the long clear stretch up to the footbridge. Bring the same thing twice so you can work out whether it suits you.
https://longrunsunday.example/training/long-run-pocket-food

Hatch Loop 5K: results and splits
The timing mat at the finish worked, but the split at the half turn came from a hand clicker. Expect a few seconds' difference there. The fastest women's time was 17:42 and the last runner on the course clocked 42:11. We've put the volunteer notes under the results, including which marshal had the spare pins and how to return a chip you took home.
https://longrunsunday.example/races/hatch-loop-five

See you out there,
Mara Whitcombe, editor

Long Run Sunday · 14 Tern Yard, London E9 5DP
